item.title: 🟠 Now generally available: Discover local AI agents with Microsoft Defender
item.description:
Why this matters: Credential/phishing risk — reinforce MFA and watch for suspicious sign-ins.

As local agents have moved from experimentation into everyday work, traditional security visibility is no longer enough. Unlike static software, local agents such as coding assistants, command-line agents, desktop applications, and agentic development environments can operate on endpoints with access to a user's data, credentials, tools, and services. They can also connect to Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers that extend their access to additional tools and data. This change requires security teams to look beyond. They need to understand which local agents are running and where, which users and devices these agents are associated with, and which MCP servers these agents are configured to use.

To address this challenge, at Microsoft Build 2026, we introduced new Microsoft Defender capabilities to help security teams discover and protect more than 20 types of local AI agents. Today, discovery of AI agents and their configured MCP servers on Windows and macOS is generally available, with discovery coverage expanded to more than 50 supported agents and MCP servers. On eligible, onboarded devices, Defender discovers supported agents by observing their activity and brings the agent, device, account, and configured MCP context together to give security…

Source: Microsoft 365 Defender Blog  |  Severity: Important  |  Age: 6d

item.title: 🔵 Tracking AI adoption in North Korean threat actor tradecraft
item.description:
